events.title: The coronation of St. Edward the Confessor
events.shortBlurb: On Easter Day 1043 Edward, son of Æthelred and Emma, was crowned at Winchester, the last sainted king of the old English line…
body: On Easter Day, 3 April 1043, Edward — called the Confessor — was crowned king of the English in the Old Minster at Winchester. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records that he was consecrated 'early on Easter-day, with much pomp,' Easter falling that year on 3 April, by Eadsige, archbishop of Canterbury, assisted by Ælfric of York.

Son of King Æthelred the Unready and Emma of Normandy, Edward had passed some twenty-five years in Norman exile before being recalled in 1041, and he succeeded his half-brother Harthacnut, the last of the Danish kings, who died in June 1042. The choice of Winchester, the ancient royal city and the seat of his mother Emma, proclaimed the restored house of Cerdic after a generation of Danish rule.

His reign of twenty-three years raised his great church, Westminster Abbey, consecrated on 28 December 1065, days before his death on 5 January 1066. Miracles were reported at his tomb; Alexander III canonized him in 1161, and for centuries he was venerated as a patron of English kings.
